support.subtitle: Support the work and become a partner in spreading Torah
support.heading: Become Involved
support.lead: Judaism teaches that every person has a purpose and a role in the world, and that each of us has been given the tools and qualities fitting to realize it.
support.verse: Rejoice, O Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents
body: On this verse, Rashi brings the words of the Midrash: Zebulun and Issachar formed a partnership between them. Zebulun would dwell by the seashore, setting out to trade in ships and earn, and would provide for Issachar — who would sit and engage in Torah. Therefore Moses mentioned Zebulun before Issachar, for Issachar's Torah was made possible through Zebulun. So too it is brought in halacha, in the Tur and the Shulchan Aruch (Yoreh De'ah 246): every Jew is obligated in the study of Torah, whether poor or wealthy, whole in body or afflicted, and must set fixed times for Torah by day and by night, as it says: "You shall meditate on it day and night."

And one who is unable to learn — whether because he does not know how, or because of the pressures of life — should support those who do learn, and it will be accounted to him as though he had learned himself, as the sages expounded on the verse: "Rejoice, O Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents."

The urgent and vital national mission of our generation is to strengthen Jewish consciousness and to halt cultural and practical assimilation. The only way to do this is to teach the depth and beauty of Judaism, to reveal its wisdom and power, and thereby to restore the Jewish people's trust in their glorious heritage.

We call upon and invite everyone to whom this is important and dear, and who has the financial and organizational means, to arrange lectures, study days and Shabbatons in every Jewish community and settlement in Israel and around the world — and may it be their portion and merit in this world and the next.

Those wishing to contribute and volunteer for this important mission are welcome to contact Rabbi Yinon, who will gladly come to deliver workshops, lectures, study days and Shabbatons wherever there is demand.
